findings.reason: naming `classify_pointer` as the owner (as the landed change did) tells the implementation node to extend the one phase judgement so `/crew` cannot read a run differently from the crew live view, instead of re-deriving phase from the stream file.
findings.text: §3 states "reckon/serve.py derives a run's working phase from its stream file" and prescribes a launching phase, but the phase judgement it wants is already owned by `classify_pointer` / `_observed_phase`, whose docstring says the same call serves both `recover` and the MCP read; a node reading only the §3 text could add a second phase derivation in serve.py beside the owner, and the two would be free to disagree

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no module. It extends three existing deep mechanisms rather than spreading complexity across new wrappers: `crew.classify_pointer` / `_observed_phase` (`reckon/crew/recovery.py`), `_crew_rows` (`reckon/serve.py`), and `_north_star_rows` (`reckon/roadmap.py`).
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3's design section describes deriving a run's phase inside `reckon/serve.py` without naming the module that already owns phase classification, `reckon/crew/recovery.py:classify_pointer`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design cites the landed write path (`north_stars` in `reckon/_store.py`, commit e8efbc7) for §2, names `reckon/serve.py`'s stream-file derivation as the thing to change for §3, and leans on the existing discovery/sprint route for §4; §2 is a pure adoption of machinery that already exists — `project_state.py` validates north-stars, `roadmap.py` reports direction coverage and undeclared directions, and `serve.py`/`mcp_views.py` already return them.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no thin layer is proposed over existing machinery; §2's "read of the project resource" is the existing read, and §3/§4 change existing functions in place rather than wrapping them.
